"A single committee could not read every entry with the care it deserved," said Yvette Bouchard, awards coordinator. "People who run a business judge these entries better than we did."
How a sitting runs.
Every sitting opens with the chair going through the scoring guide with the panel, before any entry is opened. Entries are then scored one at a time, and each panel agrees on its shortlist before leaving the room.
Before you attend.
The placements now posted are provisional. Checking of entries continues to the end of February, and a panel may still be altered where a category gains or loses entries. Volunteers are asked to confirm their attendance with the awards office by February 20.
The placement notice is displayed on the members' board at the association office on Halsted Street.

Late Shopping Evenings Draw Steady Crowds
By Janet Whelan, Local Business
Shops in central Havelock stayed open until 9:00 p.m. on two evenings last week, and the Havelock Retailers' Association reports steady visitor numbers.
"Thursday was busier than any Saturday this year, and most of those who came in had never visited us," said Arnold Deming, who keeps a bookshop on Priory Lane.
The blocks did not trade on the evenings first published. The South Block shops opened late on Wednesday, October 8, and the North Block on Thursday, October 9, the members having agreed to exchange the two dates. Every participating shop appeared in a leaflet delivered across the town.
The association, which meets on the last Tuesday of each month, has forty-one members, and thirty-four opened on one of the two evenings. Printing and delivery were divided among them by frontage. Officers say a further promotion is planned, but no date is fixed.
